I was thinking about the context of the quote whether it were a speech or a text. I'd like to place it in the full thought.

I can't seem to find where the quote originates from. It seems it has been falsely attributed to Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn in order to play off of his popularity. As such the original context of the quote is muddled in mystery.

In full thought I like to think of the Olympics. It not only takes super-human levels of hard work and dedication in order to be able to win a medal in one of the competitions, but it also requires a sort of genetic lottery. Those whose genes are more suitable for the competition at hand have a far greater chance of winning, almost no matter how much effort the competition puts in. This is an example where although everyone is free to compete, not everyone can make the cut. Equal effort does not always have an equal outcome.

Of course you could always measure people's genetic differences and impose penalties on those who had better luck with the genetic lottery in order to try and balance out the outcomes of the competition if somehow in practice this made the competition more "fair" but why should any one individual be shackled for something outside of their control?

No matter what side you're on this sort of thing should be important. Sources. Context. Facts. Seek proof even if it sounds right. If it isn't important to you should rethink the way you approach politics.
